description: The GeoAsset project of the Spatial Finance Initiative, hosted by the UK Centre for Greening Finance and Investment, creates open asset-level databases for high-impact industries by collecting openly available information on physical assets, such as location, ownership and capacity, and aggregating it in standard templates. Its aim is to link geolocated assets to their owners so that geospatial analysis can be attributed to companies and to financial instruments such as loans, bonds and listed equities. It uses manual and machine-learning analysis of satellite, geospatial and web data. On 26 September 2026 the databases page offered cement (3,117 plants worldwide), iron and steel (1,598 plants), pulp and paper (3,403 facilities), petrochemicals (342 ethylene plants), salmonid marine aquaculture (3,478 facilities), beef abattoirs of the five largest meatpackers (119), wastewater treatment plants in Europe (1,490) and agriculture in England (117,000 farming entities), each with a free download. No licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: each database is a snapshot at its publication date, and ownership is reported only where it could be traced. For simulation it provides ownership-linked asset inventories of heavy industry for hazard exposure, supply-chain and climate risk studies of industrial plants and their financiers. Related catalogue records include the Global Iron and Steel Tracker, the Global Cement and Concrete Tracker and Climate TRACE.
